edits.hebrew: דלהדי ביזעא שרי – אף בשתיה, דמירתת ולא נגע.

edits.english: Opposite the crack, it is permitted - even for drinking, as he would be afraid and would not touch it.

edits.hebrew: דהאי גיסא והאי גיסא אסור – אף בהנאה. וכשאין נתפס על כניסתו כגנב, עסקינן שהיה לו חלק ביין, דאי נתפס עליו כגנב, כוליה שרי. ואית דגרסי: הוו ביזייני בדשא – חורין, וסדקין, ובקיעין. ובקעהו תרגומו: ובזעהו.

edits.english: On this side and that side, it is forbidden - even for benefit. We are dealing with a case where he is not caught as a thief upon his entry, as he had a share in the wine. For if he were caught as a thief, all of it would be permitted. And some versions read: 'There were *bizaynei* in the door' - holes, cracks, and fissures. And 'he split it' (בקעהו) its Aramaic translation is 'ובזעהו'.

edits.hebrew: ישראל בעליונה ועובד כוכבים בתחתונה – ויין בתחתונה, וישראל רואהו מלמעלה.

edits.english: A Jew in the upper story and a gentile in the lower story - and the wine is in the lower story, and the Jew sees it from above.

edits.hebrew: שרי – כל שרי דהכא, שרי אף בשתיה, דהא לא נגע קאמרינן. וכל אסיר דהכא, אף בהנאה. ובכולהו, הלכתא כרבא.

edits.english: Permitted - every 'permitted' here means permitted even for drinking, as we say he did not touch it. And every 'forbidden' here means forbidden even for benefit. And in all of these cases, the *halakha* is in accordance with Rava.

edits.hebrew: אי אית ליה לאישתמוטי – ולומר: לכך נכנסתי, סמכא דעתיה ולא מירתת. דכי על להך ביתא מעיקרא, אדעתא דלנסוכי על, וסבר: אי משכחו לי, אשתמיטנא. ואע"ג דבמגע היין לית ליה לאשתמוטי, אסור. דאי לאו לנסוכי על, למה ליה דעייל? ולא דמי למניח עובד כוכבים בחנותו, דהתם, דכיון דברשות עייל, וידעינן למאי עייל, כל זמן שלא הודיעו שמפליג, מותר, דסבר: אי נגענא, השתא אתי וחזי לי.

edits.english: If he has a way to excuse himself - and to say: 'I entered for this reason,' his mind is at ease and he is not afraid. For when he entered this house initially, he entered with the intention to pour a libation, and he thought: 'If they find me, I will excuse myself.' And even though he has no excuse for touching the wine, it is forbidden. For if he did not enter to pour a libation, why did he enter? And it is not similar to leaving a gentile in his store, for there, since he entered with permission and we know why he entered, as long as he did not inform him that he was leaving for a long time, it is permitted, for he thinks: 'If I touch it, he will come now and see me.'

edits.hebrew: ואי לית ליה לאישתמוטי – שרי, וכיון דבהול הוא על כניסתו, מירתת ולא נגע.

edits.english: And if he does not have a way to excuse himself - it is permitted. And since he is anxious about his entry, he is afraid and does not touch it.

edits.hebrew: ננעל הפונדק – ונתייחד עובד כוכבים עם היין, או שאמר ישראל לעובד כוכבים: שמור, עמוד מבחוץ ושמור.

edits.english: The inn was locked - and the gentile was secluded with the wine, or the Jew said to the gentile: 'Guard it, stand outside and guard it.'

edits.hebrew: אסור – דחיישינן דלמא על, כיון דאמר לו: שמור, סמכא דעתיה דמפליג מיניה.

edits.english: Forbidden - for we are concerned that perhaps he entered, since he said to him: 'Guard it,' his mind was at ease that the Jew was leaving him.

edits.hebrew: שמע ישראל קל צלויי – ודוקא היין שעל הדולבקי שרי, כדתנן במתני'. ורבא קא משמע לן דקל צלויי כלא הודיעו שמפליג דמי. אי נמי, שאפילו על השולחן מותר, ובדלא אמר לו: הוי מזוג ושותה.

edits.english: The Jew heard the sound of praying - And specifically the wine on the *dolveki* (side table) is permitted, as we learned in the Mishna. And Rava teaches us that the sound of praying is considered as if he did not inform him that he was leaving for a long time. Alternatively, even the wine on the table is permitted, provided he did not say to him: 'Mix and drink.'

edits.hebrew: שיפורא דבי שימשי – של ערב שבת, שהיו תוקעין להבדיל בין קדש לחול.

edits.english: Shofar of twilight - of Erev Shabbat, which they would blow to distinguish between the holy and the mundane.

edits.hebrew: ואי משום שבתא – ואם תאמר דסמכא דעתיה דעובד כוכבים משום דלא אתי ישראל בשבתא, האמר לי איסור גיורא כו'.

edits.english: And if because of Shabbat - And if you say that the gentile's mind is at ease because the Jew will not come on Shabbat, didn't Issur the Convert tell me etc.

edits.hebrew: פחות פחות מד' אמות – ועומד לפוש, וליכא עקירה מתחילת ד' לסוף ארבע.

edits.english: Less than four cubits at a time - and he stops to rest, and there is no continuous carrying from the beginning of four cubits to the end of four cubits.

edits.hebrew: טשא – נתחבא.

edits.english: He hid - he concealed himself.

edits.hebrew: ספק ביאה – דלא ידעינן עובד כוכבים אי על, אי לא על, טהור. ומשום הכי שרי, דשני לן ספק ביאה מביאה ודאי וספק מגע.

edits.english: Uncertainty of entry - for we do not know if the gentile entered or did not enter, it is pure. And for this reason, it is permitted, because we differentiate between uncertainty of entry and certainty of entry, and uncertainty of contact.

edits.hebrew: בקעה – שדות הרבה זו אצל זו, בימות הגשמים שזרועה היא, ואין רבים דורסין אותה, והוי רשות היחיד לטומאה, וספיקא שאירעה בה הוי ספיקא טמא.

edits.english: Valley - many fields next to each other, in the rainy season when it is sown and many people do not tread upon it, and it is considered a private domain for impurity, and an uncertainty that occurred there is an uncertainty of impurity.

edits.hebrew: וטומאה בשדה פלונית – באחת מן השדות, ואין אנו יודעין איזו היא.

edits.english: And ritual impurity in such and such a field - in one of the fields, and we do not know which one it is.

edits.hebrew: הלכתי במקום הלז – בבקעה זו.

edits.english: I walked to that place - in this valley.

edits.hebrew: ספק מגע טמא – דאמר: נכנסתי לשדה שהטומאה בה, ואיני יודע אם נגעתי בטומאה אם לאו.

edits.english: Uncertainty of contact, he is ritually impure - for he said: 'I entered the field where the impurity is, and I do not know if I touched the impurity or not.'

edits.hebrew: כיון דאיכא דפתחי חביות לשום ממונא – וכיון דחזו דחמרא הוא, פרשי, דבגניבותייהו טרידי ולא מנסכי.

edits.english: Since there are those who open barrels for the sake of money - and since they saw that it was wine, they refrained, for they are preoccupied with their thievery and do not pour libations.

edits.hebrew: הוי ספק ספיקא – ספק ישראל, ספק עובד כוכבים. ואת"ל עובד כוכבים, ספק נגע, ספק לא נגע. ובהא אפילו רבנן מודו. וכי פליגי רבנן עליה דר"א, היכי דמליא שדה טומאה, דאי על לה, לא אפשר דלא האהיל, דליכא אלא חד ספק.

edits.english: It is a compound uncertainty - it is uncertain whether they were Jews or gentiles. And even if you say they were gentiles, it is uncertain whether they touched it or did not touch it. And in this, even the Rabbis agree. And when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer, it is in a case where the field is full of impurity, for if he entered it, it is impossible that he did not overshadow it, as there is only one uncertainty.

The Gemara relates: There was an incident involving a certain gentile girl who was found among wine barrels and she was holding wine foam in her hand. Rava said: The wine is permitted, as it is reasonable to say that she took it from the outside of the barrel and not from inside the barrel. And even if there is no more of the foam on the outside of the barrel, it is reasonable to say that she happened upon the foam while it was still there, even though it is no longer there.

edits.hebrew: רביתא – תינוקת עובדת כוכבים.

edits.english: A girl - a gentile child.

edits.hebrew: אופיא – אשקומא של יין.

edits.english: Froth - wine foam.

edits.ref: Otzar Laazei Rashi, Talmud, Avodah Zarah 146
edits.english:
1909 / (Avodah Zarah 70b) / **Ophia**
Escume / escume / **FOAM**
See above no. 884.
✭ foam

edits.hebrew: אימר מגבה דחביתא שקלתה – ודוקא רביתא, דאינה יודעת בטיב ניסוך ולא מסרה נפשה למינגע. אבל גדולה, מכי חזינן דנקיטא אופיא, לא תלינן לקולא.

edits.english: Say she took it from the outside of the barrel - And specifically a young girl, who does not know the nature of libations and would not risk touching it. But for an adult woman, since we see her holding foam, we do not attribute it leniently.

edits.hebrew: אע"ג דליכא תו – שאין שם אופיא עוד, ואיכא למימר: הא ודאי בגו חביתא שקלתה.

edits.english: Even if there is no more - that there is no more foam there, and one might say: 'She certainly took it from inside the barrel.'

edits.hebrew: אימר איתרמי – דהך אופיא הוא דהואי התם.

edits.english: Say it happened to be there - that this foam was there.

edits.hebrew: פולמוסא – ראש הגייס, שר צבא.

edits.english: Pulmusa - the head of the troops, an army commander.

edits.hebrew: ולא ידענא אי – שרא משום ספק עובד כוכבים ספק ישראל, וכר"א דאמר: ספק ביאה טהור. ולקמיה פריך: הא לאו ספק ביאה הוא, דודאי עובדי כוכבים היו.

edits.english: And I do not know whether - he permitted it due to uncertainty whether they were gentiles or Jews, and in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer who says: 'Uncertainty of entry, it is pure.' And later it is asked: 'But this is not uncertainty of entry, for they were certainly gentiles.'

edits.hebrew: ישראל נינהו – ואזלינן בתר רובא, דליכא ספיקא.

edits.english: They are Jews - and we follow the majority, so there is no uncertainty.

edits.hebrew: כיון דמפתחי טובא – הרבה יותר מכדי צורך שתייתן, מוכחא מילתא דאדעתא דממונא פתחו, ובגנבותייהו טרידי ולא מנסכי. ודמי לבולשת שנכנסה לעיר בשעת מלחמה, דקתני מתניתין: אלו ואלו מותרות. הלכך, אע"ג דספק מגע הוא, כיון דמוכחא מילתא לקולא, כספק ביאה דמי.

edits.english: Since they opened many - much more than needed for their drinking, it is proven that they opened them with the intention of finding money, and they are preoccupied with their thievery and do not pour libations. And it is similar to a raiding party that entered a city during wartime, as the Mishna teaches: 'Both these and those are permitted.' Therefore, even though it is an uncertainty of contact, since the matter is proven leniently, it is considered like an uncertainty of entry.

The Gemara relates: There was an incident involving a certain tavern keeper who transferred the key [iklida] to the door of her wine shop to a gentile woman. Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Elazar said: There was a similar incident that was brought before the Sages in the study hall, and they said: She transferred to her the responsibility for safeguarding the key alone but did not authorize her to enter the tavern, so there is no concern that she entered there.

edits.hebrew: מסוביתא – מוכרת יין בחנות, כמו "זולל וסובא" (דברים כא), "סבאך מהול במים" (ישעיה א).

edits.english: Masuvita - a wine seller in a shop, like "glutton and drunkard" (Deuteronomy 21:20), "your wine is cut with water" (Isaiah 1:22).

edits.hebrew: אקלידא – מפתח, שמירת מפתחות, ולא סמכא דעתה ליכנס ונתפסה כגנב.

edits.english: Iklida - a key, for guarding keys, and her mind was not at ease to enter, and she would be caught as a thief.
Escume from Old French *escume* = foam.

edits.hebrew: יין נסך מיבעיא – בניחותא, ומסייע לרב דימי.

edits.english: Is wine for a libation necessary? - This is said with ease, and it supports Rav Dimi.
